sources.name: BEE EV Yatra snapshot, Dec 2024
sources.licence: Unclear: public GitHub copy, no licence

sources.name: MoRTH toll plazas via PM GatiShakti

assumptions.label: State EV registrations
assumptions.value: ELECTRIC(BOV) + PURE EV, cumulative and by year
assumptions.source: VAHAN4 dashboard rows in data/data.csv

assumptions.label: District EV counts
assumptions.value: State VAHAN total split in two parts. Share m = matched RTO EVs / all RTO EVs in the state (2022-2026) follows each district's matched RTO registrations; the rest (1 - m) follows 0.4 x (2W + car households) + 0.3 x power-parity households + 0.3 x VIIRS nightlights. Districts with no matched RTO get evsSource 'proxy'; state sums equal VAHAN exactly
assumptions.source: India Data Portal VAHAN by RTO (data/raw/vahan_rto/fuel.csv, HR207 dealer total excluded); proxy shares from Census 2011 and VIIRS 2024

assumptions.label: RTO to district match
assumptions.value: 1377 RTOs matched to 2021 districts by normalised name inside the state (exact, then containment, then fuzzy >= 0.8); 51% of RTOs and 79% of RTO EVs matched. Written to rto_district_crosswalk.csv
assumptions.source: Name matching only; no official RTO-to-district list was used

assumptions.label: RTO jurisdiction is not a district boundary
assumptions.value: An RTO can cover part of a district or several districts, and metro RTOs (Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai) are often named for zones, not districts. Where several RTOs match one district their EVs add; a district with an unmatched sibling RTO is under-counted and the proxy only partly corrects it
assumptions.source: RTO series start in 2022, so shares reflect recent registrations, not the earlier stock

assumptions.label: Registration place is not charging place
assumptions.value: A vehicle is counted where it is registered (often a dealer or fleet owner's city), not where it charges or runs. District EVs therefore show registration, not charging demand
assumptions.source: VAHAN registration data

assumptions.label: Official public charging stations
assumptions.source: Lok Sabha Q.453 (BHEL portal), July 2026. The jump from 29,151 (Dec 2025) most likely reflects a counting-system change, not construction

assumptions.label: Charger coverage factor per state
assumptions.value: coverageFactor = min(1, stations found / official state count), floored at 0.1. Official state count = the 29 Jul 2026 annexure for the 16 states where press confirms it (41,238), and the Dec 2025 state total scaled by 1.920 for the other 20 so the states sum to 52,718. Found stations: 31,259 (national 0.593). Ratios above 1 are capped at 1 (0 states: found data from BEE Dec 2024 / OSM exceeds the older state count); the BEE snapshot is Dec 2024 and may hold closed stations, which overstates coverage
assumptions.source: Parliament replies and PIB state counts in data/data.csv; BHEL and BEE universes differ and the series do not nest, so this is a rough scaling

assumptions.label: Urban spacing norm
assumptions.value: 1 charging station per 3 km x 3 km grid
assumptions.source: MoP Guidelines for Installation and Operation of Public Charging Infrastructure (2022, amended 2023), Location of Public Charging Stations: "At least one Charging Station shall be available in a grid of 3 Km X 3 Km. Further, one Charging Station shall be set up at every 25 Km on both sides of highways/roads."

assumptions.label: Highway spacing norm
assumptions.value: 1 charging station every 25 km on both sides of highways
assumptions.source: MoP Guidelines for Installation and Operation of Public Charging Infrastructure (2022, amended 2023), Location of Public Charging Stations: "At least one Charging Station shall be available in a grid of 3 Km X 3 Km. Further, one Charging Station shall be set up at every 25 Km on both sides of highways/roads."

assumptions.label: Coverage distance
assumptions.value: Mean distance from ~300 area-uniform sample points per district to the nearest found charger anywhere in India; within3kmShare = share of points within 3 km
assumptions.source: Not population-weighted; points over uninhabited land count equally

assumptions.label: Gap score
assumptions.value: 100 x (0.4 pct-rank EVs per adjusted charger + 0.3 pct-rank coverage km + 0.3 pct-rank modelled EVs outside 3 km); no chargers = worst rank; bands are quintiles
assumptions.source: Relative ranking across districts, not an absolute shortfall

assumptions.label: EV stock history 2014-2025
assumptions.value: 7,939,817 EVs end-2025 (BOV + pure EV)
assumptions.source: VAHAN4 dashboard, data/data.csv. 2026 excluded: partial year (data ends mid-2026). Pre-2014 stock ignored.

assumptions.label: National curve
assumptions.value: Logistic S=K/(1+exp(-r(t-t0))), r,t0 least-squares on log stock, anchored to 2025
assumptions.source: scipy fit; r=0.39, t0=2031.5 (base)

assumptions.label: Saturation stock K low/base/high
assumptions.source: Not identifiable from data before the inflection. No public policy target is in our data, so none is used as an anchor.

assumptions.label: District allocation
assumptions.value: State share drifts by 2025 momentum over 5y; districts drift half-way to state population share by 2035
assumptions.source: Assumed convergence so early-adopter districts do not compound forever.

assumptions.label: Fleet mix 2W/3W/4W
assumptions.source: VAHAN extract has no class split. Rough read of Indian EV registrations (2W and e-3W dominate).

assumptions.label: kWh per 100 km 2W/3W/4W
assumptions.source: Typical e-scooter, e-rickshaw/L5, small e-car consumption.

assumptions.label: km per day 2W/3W/4W
assumptions.source: Commuter 2W, commercial 3W, private 4W.

assumptions.label: Public charging share of energy
assumptions.source: Kazam/AEEE (80,000+ home installs): home is 80-90% of EV energy, so 10-20% is everything else, incl. workplace, depot, swap. 15% = midpoint; 20% is a ceiling. CEA FY26 metered energy implies 4-15% (report back-test, ours), and ~45% of buyers lack home charging, so no lower. Not ramped: no evidence on its trend.

assumptions.label: Utilisation (energy-based, % of 16h at rated power)
assumptions.source: 15% is a mature-network target (= 10% on 24h; IEA projects 15% for Europe by 2035, time-based). India today is 1-5% on 24h (SBI 1-3%, S&P ~5%, FICCI <2%; relayed by EMobility+/Outlook Business, originals unread) = 1.5-7.5% on 16h; 4.5% = ~3% on 24h, mid-range. Linear ramp is assumed; no source gives the path.

assumptions.label: Sensitivity on chargers to add
assumptions.value: low: public 10%, utilisation 21% (2035 value) | high: public 20%, utilisation 7.5% | EV path and all else = base; ramp applied to each
assumptions.source: Bounds from sources: public 10-20% (Kazam/AEEE residual); utilisation 21% = ChargeZone 14% restated on 16h, 7.5% = 5% on 24h (S&P, today's ceiling held flat). Computed by re-running every district; the report's 4-46 lakh is a cross-check, not an input. EV scenarios (K) are separate, not mixed in.

assumptions.label: Registered EVs: Lok Sabha vs VAHAN sum
assumptions.value: Lok Sabha 1,00,23,396 (26 Jul 2026) vs our 1.08 crore: not a conflict. Our end-2025 stock 79.4 lakh + Jan-Jul 2026 RTO registrations 18.8 lakh = ~98.2 lakh at 31 Jul (~97.4 lakh at 26 Jul), within 2-3% of official.
assumptions.source: data/data.csv VAHAN4 (BOV + pure EV; 2026 total 28.4 lakh runs to ~Oct 2026) and data/raw/vahan_rto/fuel.csv (HR207 excluded). The 1.08 crore is a later date, ~Aug-Oct 2026 adds ~9.6 lakh. Residual 2-3% unexplained (official may count other categories or differ in date); VAHAN not changed. Forecast is anchored on end-2025, so unaffected.

assumptions.label: Operating hours per day
assumptions.source: Most sites are not 24h.

assumptions.label: Rated power AC / DC30 / DC60 / DC120
assumptions.source: Nominal ratings of common unit classes.

assumptions.label: Energy share by type, urban
assumptions.source: Dense urban favours fast DC for turnover.

assumptions.label: Energy share by type, rural
assumptions.source: Lower-power units, lower grid demand.

assumptions.label: Spacing floor
assumptions.value: One charger per 2.6 x 3^2 km2 of built-up area; built-up = urban population / 5000/km2
assumptions.source: Urban spacing norm (MoP 2025, see assumptions_gap.json); density assumed. Floor chargers split AC / DC30.

assumptions.label: Connectors per station
assumptions.source: Mean of 'connectors' where reported in data/data.csv (2,572 stations: 2.07). Converts existing stations to charge points.

assumptions.label: Corridor paths are measured geometry
assumptions.value: Existing segments of each NH number from the MORTH/GatiShakti national highway layer (dated June 2022), sampled every 2 km and joined by a minimum spanning tree across holes of up to 150 km; the corridor is the tree's longest path. Length is measured on the full path; the drawn path is simplified to about 200 m. Top 18: the longest NH numbers plus major trunk routes. Segments under construction or proposed are excluded; the file has holes, so bridged stretches are straight lines. Lengths run about 5 to 12% below published figures for NH 44, 48 and 27.
assumptions.source: data/raw/roads/morth_national_highways.parquet; scripts/pipeline/04_corridors.py

assumptions.label: Charger counts as 'near' a corridor
assumptions.value: Within 5 km of the highway path (a 0.5 km sampled path, so distances are good to about 0.25 km)
assumptions.source: scripts/pipeline/04_corridors.py

assumptions.label: Highway charger spacing norm
assumptions.value: 25 km. The guideline reads 'on both sides of highways'; a station within the buffer on either side is counted as serving the corridor, so the add-count is per corridor, not per carriageway side.
assumptions.source: assumptions_gap.json norms.highwaySpacingKm

assumptions.label: Stations to add on a corridor
assumptions.value: Sum over gaps longer than the norm of ceil(gap/norm) - 1
assumptions.source: scripts/pipeline/04_corridors.py

assumptions.label: Site service radius
assumptions.value: 1.5 km (half of the 3 km urban grid cell)
assumptions.source: assumptions_gap.json norms.urbanSpacingKm

assumptions.label: Site demand points
assumptions.value: District EVs spread over up to 300 random points drawn around the district centroid (sd = quarter of the district's linear size); points within the radius of a listed charger are treated as served
assumptions.source: scripts/pipeline/04_corridors.py

assumptions.label: Site candidates
assumptions.value: OSM substation locations (grid proximity as a proxy for spare capacity) and toll plazas, inside the district; greedy maximal coverage, up to 4 sites in each of the 60 districts with the worst gap score; plus, for the 3 longest gaps on each corridor, the highway point nearest the midpoint, moved to an OSM fuel station within 300 m of the road and 2 km of the midpoint when one exists
assumptions.source: data/raw/grid/osm_substations.json; morth_toll_plazas.parquet; OSM fuel stations in data/data.csv

assumptions.label: Charger type and connectors
assumptions.value: Corridor sites dc60 (dc120 where the gap exceeds 3x the norm); urban sites dc30 if they cover 150 or more EVs, else ac; connectors ac 4, dc30 2, dc60 4, dc120 4
assumptions.source: scripts/pipeline/04_corridors.py

norms.source: MoP Guidelines for Installation and Operation of Public Charging Infrastructure (2022, amended 2023), Location of Public Charging Stations: "At least one Charging Station shall be available in a grid of 3 Km X 3 Km. Further, one Charging Station shall be set up at every 25 Km on both sides of highways/roads."

validation.check: Every district has a polygon and a data row
District population within 5% of Census 2011 total
District chargers sum to the deduplicated stations
State EV totals equal district EV totals (1%)
Every charger row maps to a district
Every site belongs to a known district
Forecast chargers required never falls 2027 to 2035
Gap band is 1-5 and consistent with score order
